title: Rabbi Binyamin bar Levi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (Of the fourth generation of Palestinian Amoraim.) He was a student of Rabbi Yochanan’s students, as at the beginning of Peah, chapter 1: “Rabbi Binyamin son of Rabbi Levi said: Rabbi Yitzchak and Rabbi Ami were sitting and raising difficulties.” In Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah, beginning of halakhah 9 of chapter 2: “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, Rabbi Chiyya in the name of Rabbi Yochanan … Rabbi Binyamin bar Livai (Hyman proposes Levi) said: Provided it was cooked like the food of Ben Drosai.”
He is mentioned in halakhah in Jerusalem Talmud Terumot, beginning of chapter 1, and 3, end of halakhah 1; Pesachim, chapter 2, end of halakhah 1; Sukkah 5:1; and Gittin 7:1.

In aggadah we find his precious words in Pesikta deRav Kahana, historical locator 137., where he said: “The boundaries of Jerusalem are destined to be full of precious stones”; in Tanchuma, Va’era 8: “If a person goes and labors in Torah and sits, I show his deeds in the world”; Esther Rabbah 2:13; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 3:4; and Vayikra Rabbah, beginning of chapter 28. Of those who speak in his name we find Rabbi Avun, as in Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 7:6 and Horayot 1:6; Rabbi Huna in his name, Esther Rabbah 2:14: “In this world, when the north wind blows, the south wind does not blow, but in the future,” etc. In Vayikra Rabbah 9:6 the statement reads “Rabbi Yose in his name”; in Bamidbar Rabbah 13:2 the reading is “Rabbi Chunya in his name”; and at the end of Shir HaShirim Rabbah, chapter 4, Hyman considers still more corrupted the reading “Rabbi Huna in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rabbi Binyamin bar Levi.”
Hyman suggests that possibly he was the son of the well-known preacher Rabbi Levi.

notes.text: Hyman’s suggested Levi parentage remains possible, not certain; his Livai-to-Levi and expanded corrupt-chain proposals are attributed. The historical Pesikta locator137. is kept without identifying its page/column system. The fourth-generation label and RabbiYochanan’s students relation follow the supplied source.

Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1 directly has Binyamin bar Levi reporting Yitzchak and Imi raising difficulties. The chapter’s unrelated Binyamin gemstone narrative was excluded from positive coverage. Hyman’s fourth-generation placement, possible Levi parentage, chain corrections and undefined historical Pesikta 137 pagination remain qualified.
